messages:
anya: quick heads-up — seeing intermittent accuracy dips on AWQ/INT8 bring-up for model-x on the summarization eval. numbers bounce between runs.
sasha: oh, details?
anya: ran per-layer/channel scans this morning. attached quick paste of the heavy hitters. copy/paste since slack files are annoying.
anya: ```
# command
python tools/outlier_scan.py --model model-x --quant awq --per-channel --topk 5 --save ./scans/run-2026-03-15.json

# sample output (layer, channel, max-activation)
layer 42: channels [12, 77, 201] max 12.46
layer 57: channels [3, 4] max 9.12
layer 120: channels [0] max 7.8
mean peak across layers: 2.4
num layers w/ peaks > 6.0: 4
``` 
anya: the big outliers are sparse but cause large quantization error in AWQ for some seeds.
sasha: eval numbers?
eval-bot: baseline FP16 rouge-l: 42.1
eval-bot: AWQ-INT8 default: rouge-l 39.0 (delta -3.1)
eval-bot: AWQ-INT8 with layer42 skipped: rouge-l 41.6 (delta -0.5)
eval-bot: AWQ-INT8 with per-channel clamp (layer42 ch12,77): rouge-l 40.8 (delta -1.3)
anya: interesting — skipping layer 42 almost recovers metric.
mike: what's the perf/cost hit for skipping a layer? is that using fp16 for that layer at runtime?
anya: yes, we fall back to fp16 execution for the skipped layer. latency increase ~6% p95 in our small microbench.
harper: that seems acceptable for high-quality routes. Could we do a cheaper clamp/scale instead of full skip?
anya: tried a hybrid: per-channel multiplicative rescale before quantization (scale factors tuned on a small calibration set). code:

```
# per-channel rescale pseudo
for ch in outlier_channels:
    weights[layer][ch] *= 0.5
# then run AWQ quantize
```

anya: result: rouge-l 41.0 (delta -1.1). better than default but worse than skip.
sasha: is the outlier persistent across prompts or seed-dependent?
anya: mostly persistent across prompts and seeds, but magnitude has variance.
mike: could we do a gated fallback: try AWQ, if per-request confidence low, route to model variant with layer-skip? or run quick KV-cache check?
harper: or use a per-client rollout where we enable skip only for enterprise customers that require quality.
anya: note: skip requires packaging change for Dedicated/private because of mixed precision in runtime. need to validate memory/provisioning.
sasha: any automated detection heuristic we can add to the bring-up pipeline? want to avoid manual scans.
anya: proposal: add a simple metric during calibration: top-3 channel peaks ratio = (max_peak / median_peak). if > 8 -> flag layer as candidate for skip or clamp.
anya: rough thresholds used:

```
flag if:
  max_peak > 6.0 OR
  (max_peak / median_peak) > 8
```

anya: pipeline step would output a skiplist like: [42, 57, 120]
sasha: can we also auto-generate per-channel clamp values? e.g. clamp 12->6, 77->4
anya: yes; compute clamp = median_peak * 4 (heuristic) and try quantize with clamps. it reduces error but sometimes underflows other channels.
mike: what about trying GPTQ for those problematic layers only? i.e., hybrid quant: AWQ everywhere except per-layer GPTQ or int8-gptq mix.
anya: tried GPTQ on layer42 only -> rouge-l 41.9 (delta -0.2), latency hit ~12%.
harper: tradeoffs: skip gives best quality, GPTQ-only layer gives near-skip quality but higher latency, clamp/rescale is cheapest but lower quality.
anya: summary suggestion for onboarding docs:
- run outlier_scan with --per-channel
- auto-flag layers using thresholds above
- try in order: per-channel clamp -> per-channel rescale -> GPTQ for layer -> skip layer (fp16)
- record latency and cost impact per option in the report

sasha: sounds good. can we instrument the console to show per-route recommended mitigation in Optimize tab?
anya: yes will open a ticket for UI bits. (will include minimal repro and example scan output)
mike: one more thing — let's add a small randomized test harness to ensure skiplist doesn't create regressions for other datasets.
anya: on it. I'll add a small swept eval across 6 datasets and run overnight; will post results tomorrow.
harper: thanks. tiny nit: add seed variability to the report so we don't overfit to one calibration seed.
anya: yes; running with 5 seeds now.
sasha: :thumbsup:
anya: posted full run: https://internal/runs/1899991234 (private link)
anya: will follow up with PR to quantization pipeline + recommended default threshold.
shan't: (reaction) :thinking_face: "
